text:
maria: Heads-up — spotting a 3x increase in premature spot evictions in us-west-2 since 03:10 UTC. Serving errors spiked, autoscale dipped, some canaries timed out.
aj: ugh. Any pattern on instance types or AZs?
maria: mostly p4d and a few a10g in az-b and az-c. Rate of interruption events from cloud metrics.
kai: is this a cloud-wide maintenance or spot-capacity reclaim? ops-bot: [alert] cloud provider: preemption wave detected in us-west-2 between 03:00-03:14 UTC, affected instance families: p4d,a10g\.
steph: we should bump min_on_demand to avoid client-facing errors while we investigate. Current mix: 15% on-demand floor, 85% spot.
aj: agree. Recommend soft floor to 35% for next 1h, then evaluate. That will cost ~+22% for the hour but avoids SLO breaches.
maria: can we do a targeted floor only for latency-sensitive routes? Example policy: 
```yaml
route_overrides:
  - route: "/v1/generate-low-latency"
    min_on_demand: 0.35
  - route: "/v1/embeddings"
    min_on_demand: 0.10
default_min_on_demand: 0.15
burst_pool_enabled: true
burst_pool_size: 0.20  # fraction of total capacity
```
aj: love that — targeted guardrails will limit cost impact.
kai: for eviction handling we should also increase eviction_credits for long-running sessions so they can survive a single preempt. current credit bucket = 2 -> set to 4 for sensitive tenants.
steph: also enable graceful preemption fallback: route to warm on-demand lanes with kv-cache transfer, not just kill. That reduces token re-gen costs.
maria: operational checklist I propose: 1) set soft min_on_demand 35% for 60m (targeted routes), 2) expand burst_pool to 25% but cap per-tenant burst to avoid noisy neighbor, 3) increase eviction_credits to 4 for tenants tagged @enterprise and @critical, 4) run canary traffic through fallback path.
aj: i can push the config as a canary to staging now, then to prod with 10% rollout.
kai: will add a short-lived capacity reservation in us-west-2 for 2h to stabilize pricing and reduce churn.
steph: monitoring: add a short-term eval that reruns prompt quality checks for the canaries — we need to surface any quality regressions from model variant fallback.
maria: logging snippet for the fallback path so SRE can trace: 
```json
{"event":"fallback_routed","request_id":"${req_id}","from":"spot-pool-azc","to":"on-demand-warm","eviction_reason":"spot_preempt","eviction_credit_left":3}
```
aj: thanks. i'll also annotate the cost dashboard with the expected delta.
ops-bot: [deploy] config-change initiated by aj at 03:45 UTC; rollout 10% -> 100% over 30m if canaries healthy.
maria: small note — let's make the soft floor revert automatically after 60m unless manual ACK; avoid lingering cost.
kai: agreed. also add a circuit-breaker if on-demand utilization > 92% to avoid total exhaustion.
steph: after we stabilize, we should sketch a permanent mixed-pool policy: dynamic floor based on 5m-avg interruption-rate + latency SLO headroom. That will be smarter than fixed floors.
aj: sounds good. i'll open a follow-up PR with the dynamic-policy pseudo-code and cost simulations.
maria: thanks team. if anyone sees errors from customers, DM me and i'll escalate. :thumbsup:
